text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran the quantized bring-up for pairwise-ranker v2 on the standard bench + production-like holdouts. Avg NDCG is about the same, but there's a ~6% drop on the 'tail-queries' slice after we started zero-padding/truncating priming. sample + logs linked: https://our-internal/drive/rlbr/v2-pad-probe :eyes:

sam: ah, wow. is that the pad/truncate change from the tokenizer switch?

maria: yeah, we switched to the new tokenizer config (drop_long_sequences=true) and canonicalized prompts to a fixed-length prefix. before: variable priming, now: pad to 512 then truncate.

jin: can you paste the slice numbers? curious if it's concentrated on very short queries or the long tail.

maria: here are the top-level numbers (float):
```
overall_ndcg: 0.712 -> 0.709
tail_ndcg: 0.634 -> 0.596  # ~5.9% relative drop
short_query_ndcg: 0.679 -> 0.672
mrr_tail: 0.423 -> 0.392
```

alex: interesting. could be that padding changes token alignment for the pairwise inputs, or the kv-cache priming offset. did you try removing priming or using left-pad vs right-pad?

maria: not yet. initial hunch: our reranker was sensitive to trailing separators in the doc field; truncation sometimes chops the anchor boundary.

tara: minimal repro: can we run a tiny ablation with (a) no pad (variable len), (b) right-pad, (c) left-pad and compare the tail slice? should be quick on dev env. i'll queue it if folks agree. :+1:

sam: agree. also try replicating on unquantized float32 to rule out quant artifacts.

maria: good call — float32 run queued (small sample). also queued left/right pad ablation on the same seed.

jin: another angle: tokenizer changes might shift subtoken boundaries for anchors vs queries, causing the model to see different anchor tokens after truncation. can you dump a few failing examples (pre/post) with tokenized view?

maria: attaching two failure examples below (pre/post).
Example 1 pre: "How to reset password?"  anchor_doc snippet tokenized: ["How"," to"," reset"," password"," ?"]
Example 1 post: "How to reset password?" anchor_doc snippet tokenized: ["How"," to"," re"," set"," password"," ?"]

alex: those subtle splits can flip attention patterns. also check pairwise ordering — if truncation removes the sentence containing the positive span and keeps surrounding garbage, score order flips.

maria: float32 smoke finished: tail_ndcg float32 stayed stable (0.635 -> 0.633). quantized still shows the drop. so it's not purely float vs int8, looks combinatorial: tokenizer pad/truncation + quantization kernel.

eval-bot: quick-eval report for run 1718463000-ablation:
- run_a (no-pad): tail_ndcg 0.637
- run_b (right-pad 512): tail_ndcg 0.597
- run_c (left-pad 512): tail_ndcg 0.600
- float32-control: tail_ndcg 0.634
(see full CSV: https://our-internal/drive/rlbr/v2-pad-ablation.csv)

tara: that pattern suggests padding alignment matters and quant kernels amplify the difference. next steps: (1) narrow down tokenizer boundary shifts on failing examples, (2) test quant kernel variants (per-channel vs per-tensor), (3) try hybrid padding heuristic (pad to nearest sentence boundary).

sam: +1. also add an eval where we keep priming variable length but set a max token budget (skip padding) — that might preserve anchor boundaries.

maria: I'll run the kernel-variant sweep and the sentence-boundary pad prototype. will post results here. thanks everyone. :sparkles:
